acme_dev: Hey support — our org credits dropped to 0 around 2026-04-01 16:00 PDT (local midnight expected). We planned jobs for after midnight PST but they were throttled. Did a reset happen early?
sarah_support: Sorry about the interruption — can you paste the tenant/org id and one request id that got a 429?
acme_dev: Tenant: org-8421. Example req id: req_9a8f3c. We expect monthly refill at 2026-04-01 00:00 America/Los_Angeles.
sarah_support: Thanks. Quick summary: our platform uses a UTC-aligned monthly reset for billing quotas; UI shows local tz conversion but there are a few edge cases with visible balance caching. Will triage. Can you confirm your org timezone setting in Console?
acme_dev: Console shows "Timezone: Account default (inferred)" — we never changed it. We assumed local midnight.
sarah_support: Got it. I'm going to run a backend check for org-8421 and look at the ledger events + token-bucket state. Quota-bot: /fetch-ledger org-8421 2026-03-31..2026-04-01
quota-bot: Fetching ledger events for org-8421... found events: REFILL 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z (+1,000,000), CONSUME spikes 2026-04-01T07:10:32Z and 2026-04-01T07:59:11Z. Note: UI cache invalidation at 2026-04-01T07:00:05Z.
acme_dev: Hmm UI cache invalidation 07:00Z is 00:00 PDT — that aligns. But our apps saw 429 at 16:00 PDT (same day) which is 23:00Z.
sarah_support: Can you share an application timeline? Did any bulk jobs run between 15:45-16:15 PDT?
acme_dev: Yes we had a cron job that ran at 15:50 PDT hitting embeddings heavy, ~3M tokens. It was within our expected burst window. We thought burst capacity would cover it until midnight local.
maria_billing: Adding context from billing — monthly refill is performed at 00:00 UTC for every tenant (backend TTL aligned to UTC month). We do expose an "Account timezone" for display only; it doesn't change the backend refill anchor. That has caused confusion before.
acme_dev: Is there any record of a refill at a different anchor for our org? Why would refill be UTC but UI show midnight PST previously?
tim_infra: Tech note: there are two clocks — backend ledger (UTC anchor) and UI conversion logic. In a small subset of tenants we saw a delayed UI cache update that showed old balance until cache eviction (this usually makes it look like you still have credits after reset). The opposite (UI showing a reset earlier) can happen if a downstream cache was primed with a zero-balance snapshot due to an unrelated rate-limit purge. We're investigating logs for org-8421.
sarah_support: For immediate remediation: 1) I've temporarily increased your burst allowance for the next 2 hours so scheduled jobs can complete (no billing change). 2) If you can pause the midnight-heavy cron for one cycle, it'll avoid hitting the fallback. 3) We're opening INC-4921 and looping in billing + infra to confirm ledger consistency and whether your tenant had an accidental early debit.
acme_dev: Thanks. Will pause the cron for tonight. Can we get a clear doc on how refill timing maps to tz and what to expect for bursts? Our SREs want deterministic scheduling.
maria_billing: Agree — we'll add a short doc snippet: "Monthly credit refill occurs at 00:00 UTC on the first of the month. Console shows converted local time based on account timezone for display only; scheduling systems should anchor to UTC to guarantee refill timing." I'll paste a draft here when ready.
tim_infra: Action items for infra: 1) Audit ledger/consumer ordering around 2026-04-01 22:00-00:00Z for org-8421. 2) Check cache priming incidents 2026-04-01T07:00Z window. 3) Add an emit in the next deploy to include X-Quota-Refill-Ts in admin logs.
sarah_support: Escalation ticket INC-4921 created and assigned to @maria_billing and @tim_infra. I'll follow up with a timeline in this thread once we have the audit.
acme_dev: Appreciate the quick action. One last question — does burst capacity have a hard daily cap that could have been exhausted earlier in the month?
maria_billing: Burst is serviced from a short-term token pool and is subject to monthly hard cap unless you have a Dedicated plan. We'll include your burst consumption in the audit output.
sarah_support: Follow-up (2026-04-01T20:14Z): infra found no early refill, but there was a large rapid consumption event at 2026-04-01T22:59:11Z UTC (15:59 PDT) that exactly exhausted the remaining monthly tokens. That aligns with your cron. We also saw a cache purge earlier that made the Console show 0 before we propagated a scheduled refill display — hence the confusion.
acme_dev: So the refill was UTC midnight but our job consumed remaining tokens earlier — makes sense. Can we get a proactive alert when balance < 5% so we can throttle?
sarah_support: Yes — we can enable low-balance webhooks for org-8421. I'll toggle that now.
acme_dev: Thanks, that should help.
sarah_support: Marking this as: root cause = heavy cron consumed final tokens before UTC refill; secondary cause = UI cache behavior increased confusion. Remediations: low-balance webhook enabled, temporary burst increase applied, doc update promised. Closing once billing verifies ledger entries.
quota-bot: INC-4921 status updated -> waiting-on-billing
last_message: maria_billing: Billing verified ledger entries and confirmed no incorrect debits. Customer notified and doc PR opened: /repos/docs/patches/123. :white_check_mark:
